quizzes.title: Checkpoint 1 — Questions and Measurement
quizzes.intro: Decision framing, units, measurement, and exploration.

questions.prompt: Data science work should start with:

options.text: A clear question tied to a decision
Deleting definitions so teams stay flexible

questions.explanation: Without a decision-focused question, analysis becomes aimless chart tourism.

wrongExplanations.a: Algorithms come after framing. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Definitions must be clearer, not vaguer. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Charts serve questions; they are not the goal.

options.text: What one row/example represents in the dataset
The same as a neural network layer

questions.explanation: Grain/unit clarity prevents invalid joins and misleading aggregates.

wrongExplanations.a: Units vary by problem. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Tools do not remove conceptual grain issues. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Model layers are unrelated to analysis units. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: How reality becomes data shapes every later conclusion

questions.explanation: Bad definitions, sensors, or labels create confidently wrong analyses.

wrongExplanations.a: Numbers need definitions and context. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Dashboards inherit measurement errors. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Missingness often biases results. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Exploratory data analysis primarily helps you:

options.text: Understand distributions, anomalies, and structure before modeling

questions.explanation: EDA surfaces quality issues and patterns that inform trustworthy next steps.

wrongExplanations.a: Quality checks are part of exploration. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Causation needs stronger designs. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Hiding uncertainty is poor practice. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: An association that may or may not be causal

questions.explanation: Association can guide hypotheses and prediction but does not prove cause alone.

wrongExplanations.a: Causation requires stronger evidence. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Experiments remain valuable. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Bias can still exist. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

quizzes.title: Checkpoint 2 — Uncertainty and Models
quizzes.intro: Sampling, modeling, evaluation, leakage, and communication.

questions.prompt: A key reason samples can mislead is:

options.text: Large n always guarantees no bias
Coverage/selection bias can omit important people or cases

questions.explanation: Who is missing from the data can distort conclusions even with large samples.

wrongExplanations.a: Size does not cure biased frames. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Rules of thumb do not erase uncertainty. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Dashboards do not magically debias. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: A predictive model is most useful when:

options.text: Features would be unavailable at prediction time
It supports an action with honest evaluation on unseen data

questions.explanation: Useful models generalize and connect to decisions under realistic constraints.

wrongExplanations.a: Unavailable features imply leakage or unusable models. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Memorization is overfitting. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Limitations belong in communication. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Data leakage is dangerous because it:

options.text: Makes offline metrics look great while real performance collapses

questions.explanation: Leaked future information inflates test scores and fails in deployment.

wrongExplanations.a: Leakage usually inflates apparent performance. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Reliability falls, not rises. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Leakage is a data/modeling issue. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: If a team can act on only the top 200 risky customers, evaluate:

options.text: Only overall accuracy on a 99% non-event class
Ranking quality / precision in the top 200 vs a baseline
Whether the model file is large

questions.explanation: Metrics should match the intervention capacity and business action.

wrongExplanations.a: Overall accuracy can hide useless rankings. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Chart color is irrelevant. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: File size is not an evaluation metric. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Only the final number with no caveats
Recommendation, evidence, uncertainty/limitations, and next measurement

questions.explanation: Decision support requires clarity about confidence and follow-up measurement.

wrongExplanations.a: Caveats are essential. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Assumptions should be explicit. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Certainty theater is dishonest. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

quizzes.title: Final Quiz — Analytical Judgment
quizzes.intro: Apply first-principles thinking to realistic scenarios.

questions.prompt: “Analyze our sales data” should first be rewritten into:

options.text: A request for more chart themes
A decision-centered question with action, timeframe, and success definition
An order to train the deepest network available

questions.explanation: Framing creates analyzable, decision-relevant work. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Themes are secondary. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Definitions are required. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Model depth without framing is cargo cult. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Customers who attend webinars renew more. Before claiming webinars cause renewals, consider:

options.text: Self-selection: attendees may already be more engaged
That experiments are impossible in business

questions.explanation: Motivated/engaged customers may both attend and renew without the webinar causing renewal.

wrongExplanations.a: Correlation is not automatic causation. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Experiments are often possible. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Definitions always matter. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Leakage because it uses future information unavailable at prediction time

questions.explanation: At prediction time you do not know days until a future cancellation.

wrongExplanations.a: It would not be available in true production scoring.
wrongExplanations.c: Baselines should avoid leakage too. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Timing is central to leakage. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Class imbalance often makes raw accuracy misleading because:

options.text: Predicting the majority class can look accurate while missing the rare cases you care about

questions.explanation: Majority-class classifiers inflate accuracy when positives are rare.

wrongExplanations.a: Rare events often matter most. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Metrics remain essential. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Validation remains essential. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Clear questions, honest measurement, validation matched to actions, and transparent limits
Treating leakage as a performance feature

questions.explanation: First principles prioritize decisions, evidence quality, and integrity.

wrongExplanations.a: Questions come before tools. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Persuasion without uncertainty is risky. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Leakage is a defect, not a feature. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
